Layout model: blocks, pages and margins

Source: vignettes/layout-model.Rmd
layout-model.Rmd

Blocks

Everything on a bodybuildr page is a block. A block answers two questions:

  • How tall are you at this width? (measure_block())
  • Draw yourself in this box.

Text wraps to the width it gets, so its height follows:

para <- bb_text(paste(rep("Coverage rose in most provinces.", 8), collapse = " "))
measure_block(para, width = 6)
#> [1] 0.486145703611457inches
measure_block(para, width = 2)
#> [1] 1.3890099626401inches

Some blocks have no height of their own. A plot without a height, a bb_spacer() without a height and a bb_placeholder() are flexible: they take the height their container gives them.

measure_block(bb_spacer(), 3)
#> [1] NAinches

Anything you pass where a block is expected goes through as_block(): strings become bb_text(), ggplots bb_plot(), image paths bb_image(), grobs bb_grob().

Composing

bb_stack() places blocks top to bottom; bb_cols() side by side. Widths are passed down and heights come back up, so nothing needs a hand-set height.

row <- bb_cols(
  bb_table(list(list("Total population", "45,696,159"),
                list("Surviving infants", "530,193")),
           widths = c(2, 1), align = c("left", "right")),
  bb_stack(bb_text("Notes", style = "subheading"),
           bb_text("A second column with its own stack.", style = "note"),
           gap = unit(4, "pt")),
  widths = unit(c(4, 1), c("in", "null")),   # 4 in, then the rest
  gap = 0.25
)
measure_block(row, width = 7.5)
#> [1] 0.625inches

In a row, flexible children (a plot, a placeholder) stretch to the tallest fixed sibling. Tables placed side by side can share row heights with sync_rows = TRUE, so their dividers line up.

Pages

A page_template() holds the page size, margins, header and footer. A bb_page() stacks its blocks in the space between them. The footer is anchored to the bottom margin, so it lands in the same place on every page, however much content sits above it.

template <- page_template(
  margin_x = 0.5, margin_top = 0.3, margin_bottom = 0.3,
  header = bb_running_header("Annual report", "{country}"),
  footer = bb_page_footer("Organisation", "{page} / {pages}")
)

page <- bb_page(
  bb_section_header("Overview", refs = "[1]"),
  row,
  bb_box(bb_text("Flat grey note panel.", style = "note"), box_style_panel()),
  template = template,
  gap = c(0.08, 0.2),
  data = list(country = "Argentina")
)

page_layout(page)[c("available", "used", "free")]
#> $available
#> [1] 9.26375
#> 
#> $used
#> [1] 1.707813
#> 
#> $free
#> [1] 7.555938

page_layout() reports the space without exporting. If content outgrows the body, export_pdf() warns with the overflow in inches.

A bb_document() numbers its pages after dropping NULLs, so an optional page shifts every later “n / N” automatically:

optional_page <- NULL
doc <- bb_document(page, optional_page, bb_page("Second page", template = template,
                                                data = list(country = "Argentina")))
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
export_pdf(doc, f)

Three spacing bands

Spacing is set in three separate places, and none of them affects the others:

  1. Page margins: page_template(margin_x, margin_top, margin_bottom). A full-bleed block, such as bb_banner(), spans the full page width instead (and sits flush with the top edge when it is the header).
  2. Layout gaps: gap in bb_stack(), bb_cols() and bb_page().
  3. Box spacing: padding and margin of box_style() in bb_box().

Themes and text styles

A theme defines the palette and the text roles (body, note, section, table_header, …). Components default to a role, and a text_style() only lists what it changes:

th <- bb_theme(font = "sans", base_size = 9,
               colors = list(primary = "#0C2C5E", accent = "#E5782A"))
bb_set_theme(th)

bb_text("Semibold, muted", style = text_style(weight = 600, color = "muted"))
#> <bb_text>
bb_text("Note role, italic", style = text_style("note", italic = TRUE))
#> <bb_text>

Weights other than 400 and 700 resolve to the installed face (for example “Source Sans 3 Semibold”) when systemfonts finds one, and fall back to bold or regular otherwise.
